name: fifteen-hours
title: A Guardsman Lasts 15 HOURS... This One Had 1 Left 💀 #warhammer40k
description:
First day on the front line, and the Sergeant has bad news about how long Guardsmen last. ⏱️💀

📜 THE LORE
• The Imperial Guard (Astra Militarum) is the Imperium's army: billions of ordinary humans with flak armour and a lasgun, thrown at threats that Space Marines are too few to stop.
• "15 hours" is the most famous joke statistic in the fandom: the average life expectancy of a Guardsman in combat. It shows how cheap a single soldier's life is to the Imperium.
• Commissars are political officers attached to Guard regiments. They keep morale up by any means, and they may execute soldiers on the spot for cowardice or retreat, which is why "Retreat is heresy" is no joke.
• Orks are green-skinned aliens who live for war. Their mighty charge is the "WAAAGH!", and a single Ork is far stronger and tougher than a human, so a rookie dropping one with a lasgun is a real achievement.

How long would YOU last in the Imperial Guard? 👇

name: red-wunz
title: In 40k, RED Paint Makes You FASTER (Seriously) 🔴 #warhammer40k
description:
An Ork Mek paints his buggy red, and it really goes faster. 🔴💨

📜 THE LORE
• Orks give off a psychic field without knowing it. When enough Orks believe something, that shared belief bends reality, so Ork guns made of scrap still fire and their junk machines still run.
• "Red wunz go fasta" is the most famous example: Orks believe red vehicles are faster, so red vehicles really are faster. The Evil Sunz clan, obsessed with speed, paint everything red for this reason.
• Meks (Mekboyz) are the Ork engineers who build and "improve" their vehicles and weapons, mostly by instinct.
• It only works for Orks. A human painting his tank red gets nothing, unless the Orks decide it belongs to them.
• To the Imperial Guard, leaving the battlefield without orders is desertion, a crime the Commissars punish without mercy.

What's the most ridiculous Ork logic that actually works? 👇

name: ogryn-loyal
title: OGRYNS Can't Count... But They NEVER Leave You 😢 #warhammer40k
description:
A giant Ogryn is ordered to protect the rookie. He takes it VERY seriously. 🛡️😢

📜 THE LORE
• Ogryns are abhumans: huge, tough humans who evolved on harsh, high-gravity worlds. They stand 2.5 to 3 metres tall and the Imperial Guard uses them as shock troops.
• They are not clever (many can barely count), but they are famously loyal and almost never break, which makes up for it.
• Ogryns often serve as bodyguards, and Bullgryns carry huge slab shields that lock together into a walking wall of cover.
• The smartest Ogryns get a brain-boosting treatment called B.O.N.E. and become "Bone'eads", the sergeants of Ogryn squads.
• Ogryns love "da Emperor" with all their heart. An Ogryn not knowing what "the Guard" is while serving in it is a fan joke, not canon.

Would YOU trust an Ogryn bodyguard? 👇

name: golden-throne
title: The Emperor Sat 10,000 Years. Here's the Cost 💀 #warhammer40k
description:
The sergeant explains what the Emperor has been doing for ten thousand years. The rookie wants a shift. 🕯️💀

📜 THE LORE
• The Emperor of Mankind was mortally wounded by his son Horus at the end of the Horus Heresy, about 10,000 years before the 41st Millennium. His broken body was placed on the Golden Throne, a huge life-support machine, and has sat there ever since.
• The Throne keeps him barely alive. Psykers are sacrificed to it to feed it with psychic power; "a thousand a day" is the famous figure from the lore.
• His mind powers the Astronomican, a psychic beacon that lets Navigators steer starships through the Warp. Without that "light", ships get lost and the Imperium falls apart.
• Commissars say "The Emperor protects" constantly, and the Imperium treats it as faith, not a question.
• The 15-hour Guardsman joke is a fan meme, not canon. The commissar's put-down is that joke, so he is saying even a short shift on the Throne would break the rookie.

Would YOU take a shift on the Golden Throne? 👇

name: krieg-debt
title: Krieg's World Burned. Its Soldiers Still Die for Him 💀 #warhammer40k
description:
A whole planet rebelled against the Emperor and lost. Its survivors now die for him on purpose. 💀

📜 THE LORE
• Krieg was an Imperial world that rebelled against the Imperium over its heavy tithe demands. The civil war dragged on for about five hundred years, and the planet ended up a poisoned, nuclear-scarred wasteland.
• The survivors became the Death Korps of Krieg, Imperial Guard regiments that serve as penance for their world's rebellion. They see dying in the Emperor's service as the way to atone.
• They are famous for gas masks, long greatcoats, grim trench-warfare tactics, and total fearlessness: a Kriegsman will march into any fire. (Source: Warhammer 40,000 Imperial Guard codex lore; Lexicanum "Death Korps of Krieg".)
• Commissars are the officers who enforce discipline in the Guard. Krieg regiments rarely need that, since they are not afraid of death.
• "Krieg just keeps the receipt" is a fan joke for the penance idea, not canon. The 15-hour Guardsman meme is also fan lore.

Send this to the friend who thinks the Guard fights for glory. 💀

name: deathwatch-vigil
title: One Silver Arm: Why Deathwatch Marines Wear Half 💀 #warhammer40k
description:
Space Marines would die for their Chapter. In the Deathwatch, they wear it on one shoulder. 💀

📜 THE LORE
• The Deathwatch is the Ordo Xenos' own Space Marine force: Marines are lent out ("seconded") by their home Chapters to hunt aliens for the Inquisition. They fight in small mixed kill-teams.
• Their armour is black, with a silver left shoulder pad marked with the Inquisitorial "I" and skull. The right shoulder pad keeps the colours and symbol of the Marine's home Chapter (here: Space Wolves, Black Templars, Blood Angels).
• The Marines in the comic wear different armour marks: Mk VII Aquila (Space Wolf), Mk X Tacticus (Black Templar) and an older Mk VI Corvus (Blood Angel veteran).
• Service is called the Long Vigil. Many Marines serve for years, and plenty never go back to their Chapter. (Source: Warhammer 40,000 Deathwatch codex lore; Lexicanum "Deathwatch".)
• "Half a Marine goes home, the other half stays on the Vigil" is a fan line for the idea, not canon. Not checked live on Lexicanum this run.

name: deathwatch-tarsis
title: To Kill a Billion Tyranids, They Needed ONE 💀 #warhammer40k
description:
To kill a billion Tyranids, the Deathwatch needed just one of them. Alive. 💀

📜 THE LORE
• The Battle of Tarsis Ultra (Third Tyrannic War): Inquisitor Fidus Kryptman's Deathwatch team captured a live Lictor (Lexicanum: Battle of Tarsis Ultra, Kryptman).
• Magos Vianco Locard built a biological poison from the Lictor's genetic makeup (Lexicanum: Vianco Locard).
• Deathwatch Captain Bannon (Imperial Fists) died on an earlier mission, so Uriel Ventris of the Ultramarines took command of the final assault (Lexicanum: Bannon, Uriel Ventris).
• Ventris boarded the last hive ship and infected the Norn Queen; the chain reaction killed the remaining Tyranids on the planet (Lexicanum: Vianco Locard).
• The dialogue and the exact boarding scene are fan dramatisation of the real events.

Which Chapter would you want on your kill-team? 👇
